public_rationale: CoreWeave's own filing describes the March 2025 OpenAI deal. OpenAI's payments are subject to CoreWeave meeting delivery and availability requirements, and OpenAI can cancel if CoreWeave repeatedly fails. CoreWeave said it intended to fund the build with new debt in a special vehicle, so the financing was not yet in place. In July 2025 it closed a $2.6 billion loan specifically to deliver the OpenAI contract. That matches his chain: expansion needed new loans, those loans were tied to the contract, and the contract depends on delivering capacity. By August 2025, CoreWeave said its cash plus available borrowing covered a year of obligations. That counts loans raised after the post, and the same filing says future investment may need significant debt or equity, so it does not undo the March position.
limitations: The IPO prospectus and Q1 10-Q could not be read, so the March 2025 position rests on later filings describing the March agreement.
Graded on the narrower reading (no funds for the specific expansion), not general illiquidity.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: CoreWeave lacks the liquidity to expand as required, and further loans depend on contracts that themselves depend on that expansion.

statement.excerpt: It currently lacks the liquidity to do so, and further loans will be contingent on its contracts, which are contingent on CoreWeave's ability to aggressively expand.
statement.document_title: The Phony Comforts of AI Optimism

from_speaker: To service the revenue that OpenAI will bring, CoreWeave is required to aggressively expand
It currently lacks the liquidity to do so
further loans will be contingent on its contracts
which are contingent on CoreWeave's ability to aggressively expand
our_interpretation: 'Lacks the liquidity to do so': CoreWeave did not have the cash or committed financing on hand to fund the expansion needed for the OpenAI contract, so that expansion depended on new borrowing. It does not mean CoreWeave could not pay its existing bills.
'Further loans will be contingent on its contracts': new loans to fund the build were tied to, or secured by, specific customer contracts such as OpenAI's.
'Contracts contingent on ability to expand': customer payments depend on CoreWeave delivering the promised capacity, and customers can cut commitments if it fails.

Target period: March 2025 ('currently', the post date) through 24 March 2026. The claim speaks of further loans to come, and his context frames the situation over 'the next year'. Evidence about the March 2025 OpenAI agreement and the loans that followed falls in this window.
criteria.support_condition: CoreWeave disclosures show that the OpenAI expansion was to be funded by new debt not yet in place in March 2025, that such debt was tied to the OpenAI contract, and that OpenAI's payments depend on CoreWeave delivering capacity.
criteria.contradiction_condition: CoreWeave already had cash or committed financing to fund the OpenAI expansion in March 2025; or its new loans were not tied to customer contracts; or its customer commitments did not depend on delivery.

evidence.excerpt:
In the event of the Company’s repeated failure to meet availability of service requirements,
OpenAI has the right to terminate all or a portion of the committed amount. Under the outstanding order submitted pursuant to the Commercial Agreement, the Company has established a special
purpose vehicle that will hold the infrastructure, and the Company intends for the special purpose vehicle to incur indebtedness to finance its obligations under the Commercial Agreement.
evidence.locator: Notes to financial statements, 'Strategic Customer Agreement'
evidence.explanation: The OpenAI agreement signed in March 2025 depends on CoreWeave delivering capacity, and OpenAI can terminate if CoreWeave fails. CoreWeave planned to fund the build with new debt in a special vehicle. This matches each link of the claimed chain.

evidence.excerpt: today announced it has closed a $2.6 billion delayed draw term loan facility (“DDTL 3.0 Facility”), continuing the company’s investment in world-class infrastructure tailored for artificial intelligence. The funding will be used to support the purchase and maintenance of advanced equipment, hardware, and cloud infrastructure systems to deliver services under a long-term agreement with OpenAI.
evidence.explanation: The next loan after the post was raised specifically to deliver the OpenAI contract. This shows further loans were tied to that contract and the expansion needed new debt.

evidence.excerpt:
We believe our existing balance of cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments, in addition to amounts available for borrowing under our various debt agreements, will be sufficient to
